headline: Methods bridge sparse cancer measurements with external references or complementary modalities
label: Cross Modal Cancer Inference
summary: Seven preprints pair cfDNA, scRNA-seq, histology and molecular data with external references to improve cancer detection, survival and clone inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supplementing a limited primary measurement with an external reference or a second modality. mFrag weights cfDNA fragmentomic features using external DNA methylation atlases for lung cancer early detection. EvoSurv adds a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation to clinical and RNA data for survival modeling. OmniT2I renders molecular profiles as images, fuses them with histopathology embeddings, and predicts missing modalities. KLONE assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones using cross-modal similarity. The 1.3M-slide H&E mapping shows that sex, age group and self-reported race are recoverable from foundation-model features, a caution about confounding. scBoost and scDNM, which address cell-type classification, are peripheral to this thread.
